
'''Alberto Oliverio''' (born 1 December 1938) is a [[biologist]] and psycho-biologist. He is currently professor of [[Psychobiology]] at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]]. He has been one of the main assistants of Nobel prize winner [[Daniel Bovet]].<ref>Bovet, D., Bovet-Nitti, F., & Oliverio, A. (1969). Genetic aspects of learning and memory in mice. Science.</ref><ref>Bovet, D., McGaugh, J. L., & Oliverio, A. (1966). Effects of post trial administration of drugs on avoidance learning of mice. Life Sciences, 5(14), 1309-1315.</ref> 

==Publications==
Oliverio is author or co-author of about 400 publications. He is author of about 30 chapters or general reviews in edited books or annual reviews. Has edited 6 books on animal behavior and [[behavioral genetics]] and is the author of many books on memory, brain and behavior.
 
==Research fields==
Neurochemical – neurophysiological correlates of memory. Genetic approaches to behavior.
